money.note: Individuals gave $88,497; PAC money $6,000; candidate's own money $6,712. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Communications professional and founder of Hyperfocused Communications (launched 2022), offering media relations and content marketing. Earlier worked on NYC Broadway Week. Hofstra University graduate (2014). Single mother from the Jersey Shore. First-time candidate who has held no public office.

endorsements.text: In her Ballotpedia survey she lists endorsements from New Jersey Citizen Action, Monmouth County Democrats, Ocean County Democrats, Jackson Democrats, Derel Stroud and Julie Flynn (self-reported). She also lists Moms Demand Action's Gun Sense Candidate Distinction, which she notes is not an endorsement.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions from her on data centers, property taxes, development and land protection, foreign or investor ownership of homes and land, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. She has never held public office, so there is no governing record to review. Her town of birth is not given. Her claims that she pushed county commissioners and state lawmakers on health programs and hurricane costs come only from her campaign site, and we found no independent record of them. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or land-use statements about her.

cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for New Jersey's 4th District since January 1981. Born in Rahway, NJ. Business administration degree from Trenton State College (1975). Worked in his family's sporting goods business and as executive director of New Jersey Right to Life. Chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee in 2025-26.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by President Donald Trump for the 2026 election, per Ballotpedia.
Campaign site says he received unanimous endorsements from the Ocean County GOP and Monmouth County GOP for reelection in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Smith grew up beyond his attending high school in Perth Amboy, or when he first lived in New Jersey. We found no documented statements or actions by him on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, restrictions on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, growth and land-use limits, school choice or teacher pay, or police pay and pensions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so there is no questionnaire on his positions. Some sections of the Ballotpedia and Wikipedia pages were cut off before the end, and we left out anything we could not read.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: U.S. House member since 1981 (about 45 years), including four years as Veterans' Affairs Committee chairman (2001-2005) and current Foreign Affairs Committee chair. Earlier he worked in his family's sporting goods business and as executive director of New Jersey Right to Life.
qual.why: Decades of actual legislative office in Washington, with a long record of authoring and passing bills and handling constituent casework, fits the lawmaking, oversight and constituent-service job at the top of the rubric.
qual.label: Decades of actual legislative office in Washington, with a long record of authoring and passing bills and handling constituent casework, fits the lawmaking, oversight and constituent-service job at the top of the rubric.

pro-life.evidence: Introduced the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion Act in several forms starting in 2011; the 2013 version further restricted insurance coverage of abortion and passed the House but was not voted on by the Senate.

second-amendment.evidence: Co-sponsored a ban on bump stocks with Rep. Leonard Lance after the 2017 Las Vegas shooting.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain people in the U.S. illegally who are arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting; it became law January 29, 2025.
